testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If you plan to stop on the road to unload cargo, what should you do?

options.text: Stop suddenly since you are already on the road.
Tap your brakes to warn other drivers.
Wave your arm out the window to get other drivers' attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brakes to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Tap your brakes and flash your brake lights to warn other drivers when you plan to slow down or stop where they may not expect it. Use this method when stopping on the road to unload cargo or passengers.

questions.question: When will your CDL be revoked?

options.text: When you want to add an endorsement.
When your regular driver's license is revoked.
When you have not paid a toll.

questions.correctAnswerText: When your regular driver's license is revoked.
questions.explanation: If your regular driver's license is revoked, canceled, or suspended because of moving traffic violations, you will also lose your CDL. This does not apply if your license is revoked for parking violations.

questions.question: If the coolant temperature gauge goes above the highest safe level, what should you do?

options.text: Keep driving.
Pull over and check what is wrong.
Turn on the air conditioner.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check what is wrong.
questions.explanation: If the coolant temperature gauge goes too high, stop driving as soon as you safely can and find out what is wrong. Your engine could fail or catch fire.

questions.question: Why do some air brake systems add alcohol to the system?

options.text: To make the brakes work without squeaking.
To prevent ice from forming in the brake system.
To prevent people from breathing the air from the system.

questions.correctAnswerText: To prevent ice from forming in the brake system.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. This adds alcohol to the system to help prevent ice from forming in cold weather.

questions.question: What is blocking used for?

options.text: To keep cargo from shifting.
To keep cargo from being loaded too high.
To keep cargo from being unloaded too quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep cargo from shifting.
questions.explanation: Blocking is placed in front, behind, and on the sides of cargo to stop it from sliding while the vehicle moves.

questions.question: When the examiner asks you to change lanes during the driving test, what should you do?

options.text: Change lanes right away without looking.
Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
Change lanes as fast as possible, even if you cut off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, you will be asked to change lanes. Check traffic carefully and use your signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: What happens if an engine does not have the right amount of oil?

options.text: The vehicle will have trouble stopping.
The vehicle will make quick, jerking movements while driving.
The engine can be damaged very quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine can be damaged very quickly.
questions.explanation: Your engine needs enough oil pressure to work properly. An engine can be destroyed fast if it runs without oil.

questions.question: When can mirrors be checked properly?

options.text: When the trailer is straight.
When there is no trailer.
When the vehicle is on a slight incline.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the trailer is straight.
questions.explanation: On a vehicle with trailers, mirrors can only be adjusted correctly when the trailers are straight. Check mirror adjustment before every trip.

questions.question: Why should you do pre-trip inspection steps in the same order each time?

options.text: You will be less likely to forget to check something.
It will be faster.
It is required by law.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be less likely to forget to check something.
questions.explanation: Do pre-trip inspections the same way every time. This helps you remember all the important steps and not skip anything.

questions.question: When driving at highway speeds, how far ahead should you watch the road?

options.text: One block
100 yards
A quarter mile

questions.correctAnswerText: A quarter mile
questions.explanation: Watch the road 12 to 15 seconds ahead of your vehicle to spot obstacles and dangers early. At highway speeds, this distance is about a quarter mile.

questions.question: Water on a roadway can cause:

options.text: Hydroplaning.
Acceleration.
Stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hydroplaning.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when water collects on the road surface.

questions.question: A trailer brake hand valve can be used to:

options.text: Add fuel to the truck.
Stop the truck from rolling back when starting from a stop.
Check the engine oil level.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the truck from rolling back when starting from a stop.
questions.explanation: The trailer brake hand valve stops the vehicle from rolling back when you start it from a stop.

questions.question: When checking tires, which is NOT a concern?

options.text: Too much air pressure.
Front tires with at least 4/32 inch of tread.
Using radial and bias-ply tires together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Front tires with at least 4/32 inch of tread.
questions.explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch. Do not mix radial and bias-ply tires or use tires of different sizes.

questions.question: While driving, a driver should:

options.text: Not worry about what is happening on the sides of the vehicle.
Watch what is happening on all sides of the vehicle.
Not worry about what is happening behind the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch what is happening on all sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: You must watch all sides of your vehicle at all times. Check your mirrors regularly while driving.

questions.question: A jogger wearing headphones:

options.text: Is probably aware of what is happening around them.
May not be aware of what is happening around them.
Can hear traffic sounds.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not be aware of what is happening around them.
questions.explanation: Be careful around pedestrians, joggers, and cyclists wearing headphones. They may not hear your vehicle and could do something dangerous.

questions.question: Why do large vehicles use air brakes?

options.text: Other brake systems are too loud.
Air brakes work very well.
Other brake systems are hard to find.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air brakes work very well.
questions.explanation: When used and maintained properly, air brakes are a safe and effective way to stop large, heavy vehicles.

questions.question: Starting a left turn before reaching the center of an intersection may:

options.text: Complete the turn without problems.
Hit other vehicles with the left side of your vehicle.
Make other drivers move for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hit other vehicles with the left side of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Reach the center of the intersection before you turn left. Turning too soon can cause your vehicle to swing into other vehicles.

questions.question: Wheels with welding repairs:

options.text: Are safe if a professional did the work.
Are safe if the repair looks solid.
Are not safe to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are not safe to use.
questions.explanation: Do not use wheels or rims with welding repairs. Replace them before driving the vehicle.

questions.question: After changing a tire, you should:

options.text: Stop soon to check that the lug nuts are tight.
Repair the brakes.
Let air out of the tire to 10 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop soon to check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: Stop a short time after changing a tire to recheck that the lug nuts are tight.

questions.question: The faster you drive:

options.text: The shorter your stopping distance will be.
The longer your stopping distance will be.
The easier it will be to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer your stopping distance will be.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase your stopping distance. Brake accordingly.

questions.question: If there is a fire in your vehicle and you do not know how to put it out, what should you do?

options.text: Use a fire extinguisher.
Try to put out the flames with water.
Move away from the fire and wait for firefighters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move away from the fire and wait for firefighters.
questions.explanation: If you do not know how to put out a fire, do not try. Move away and wait for firefighters to arrive. Let them handle it. This is especially important for fires involving hazardous materials.

questions.question: When making a tight turn in a CMV, the driver should:

options.text: Drive as fast as a car driver would.
Not worry about speed, only focus on the road.
Brake early and slow down gradually to warn drivers behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake early and slow down gradually to warn drivers behind.
questions.explanation: Drivers behind you may not expect how slowly a CMV must go to make a tight turn safely. Brake early and slow down gradually to warn them in advance.

questions.question: A ____ lets a driver apply spring brakes slowly and smoothly.

options.text: Modulating control valve
Trailer air supply control
Relay valve

questions.correctAnswerText: Modulating control valve
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets a driver apply spring brakes slowly. In vehicles with this feature, a lever on the dashboard controls the valve.

questions.question: To know if your vehicle can carry a load safely, you must know:

options.text: The vehicle's suspension rating.
The tire rating for the front tires only.
The tire rating for the rear tires only.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle's suspension rating.
questions.explanation: It is your job to make sure your vehicle is not overloaded. Know the legal weight limits and the maximum weight your vehicle can carry, including the suspension system's weight capacity.

questions.question: What is the Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR)?

options.text: The loaded weight of a single vehicle as stated by the manufacturer
The maximum weight that can be pulled by a vehicle
The minimum weight that can be hauled by a vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: The loaded weight of a single vehicle as stated by the manufacturer
questions.explanation: The Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) is the loaded weight of a single vehicle as stated by the manufacturer.

questions.question: When driving a 50-foot truck at 50 mph, the minimum following distance should be:

options.text: Four seconds.
Five seconds.
Six seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Six seconds.
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, allow one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At higher speeds, use the same formula and add one more second.

questions.question: Before a trip, you should check that:

options.text: The brake pedal sticks.
The gas pedal is loose.
The grooved pedal surface has not been worn smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The grooved pedal surface has not been worn smooth.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip check, make sure nothing blocks the pedals. Check that the pedals work properly and that the grooved surfaces on the pedals are not worn smooth.

questions.question: Alcohol leaves the body:

options.text: By exercising.
At a fixed rate.
More quickly if the person stays awake.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a fixed rate.
questions.explanation: The liver removes alcohol from the body at a fixed rate. Coffee or cold showers will not speed this up. The only way to become sober is to give your body time to remove the alcohol.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, the heaviest cargo should be placed:

options.text: On top of the lighter cargo.
Under the lighter cargo.
At the rear of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under the lighter cargo.
questions.explanation: Avoid making vehicles top-heavy if possible. A top-heavy vehicle is more likely to roll over. Place the heaviest items on the bottom and lighter items on top.

questions.question: When driving on a wet road, you should reduce your speed by:

options.text: About one-half.
About one-third.
About one-quarter.

questions.correctAnswerText: About one-third.
questions.explanation: Slow down when driving on surfaces with less traction. Reduce your speed by about one-third on wet roads.

questions.question: When does alcohol start to affect the body?

options.text: After just one drink.
After several drinks.
At the legal limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: After just one drink.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your muscles, reaction time, vision, and judgment. Some people show signs of impairment after the first drink. Do not drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: In bad weather, many drivers tend to:

options.text: Drive in front of trucks.
Drive to the side of trucks.
Follow trucks too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow trucks too closely.
questions.explanation: In bad weather with poor visibility, many drivers follow large trucks too closely.

questions.question: What do header boards do?

options.text: Should never be used.
Protect the driver from cargo that shifts during a crash or sudden stop.
Protect the driver's head when getting into the truck cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver from cargo that shifts during a crash or sudden stop.
questions.explanation: Header boards, also called "headache racks," stop cargo from hitting the driver if the truck crashes or stops suddenly.

questions.question: What does an air compressor governor control?

options.text: When the compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the storage tanks.
The temperature of the air pumped into the storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, the governor decides when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.

questions.question: What can happen if the exhaust system breaks?

options.text: Poisonous fumes may enter the cab.
Fumes may leak from the muffler.
Steering may become impossible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Poisonous fumes may enter the cab.
questions.explanation: Exhaust system leaks are dangerous because toxic fumes can enter the cab or sleeper, harming the driver and passengers.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, what happens if one system loses pressure?

options.text: None of the brakes will work.
Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
There is usually no noticeable effect.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
questions.explanation: If one air system loses pressure in a dual air brake system, either the front or rear brakes will stop working properly. If this happens while driving, park the truck as soon as possible.

questions.question: What is commonly found in compressed air?

options.text: Water
Cardboard
Brake fluid

questions.correctAnswerText: Water
questions.explanation: Compressed air usually contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up in the system. Tanks must be drained regularly to prevent this.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, how should you distribute the weight?

options.text: Put as little weight as possible over the axles.
Balance the weight evenly over the axles.
Do not worry about weight distribution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Balance the weight evenly over the axles.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be balanced properly. Too much weight on one axle damages it and makes steering harder. Too little weight on an axle causes poor traction and bad handling.

questions.question: What are escape ramps used for?

options.text: Only for automobiles, not trucks.
To leave the highway and enter a two-lane road.
To safely stop runaway vehicles on steep hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: To safely stop runaway vehicles on steep hills.
questions.explanation: Escape ramps are built on steep downhill roads to safely stop runaway vehicles. They have soft, loose material and sometimes slope upward.

questions.question: Which action is often best to avoid a crash?

options.text: Braking is always the best option.
Swerving may work better than braking.
Drivers should keep 100 yards between vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerving may work better than braking.
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the safest choice. You can turn to avoid an obstacle faster than you can stop.

questions.question: How can you usually stop a skid caused by pressing the gas pedal too hard?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Use the brakes.
Swerve to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Take your foot off the gas pedal to stop a skid from over-acceleration. This type of skid happens most often on snow or ice.

questions.question: When using spring brakes with a heavy load, stopping will:

options.text: Be impossible.
Take a long time.
Take a short time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a long time.
questions.explanation: Spring brakes do not work on all wheels. When spring brakes activate due to low air pressure, your vehicle needs more distance to stop, especially with a heavy load.

questions.question: If your driving test route does not include a railroad crossing, you:

options.text: Will not need to do anything about crossings.
May need to explain how to cross railroad tracks.
Will have to take a different route.

questions.correctAnswerText: May need to explain how to cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: If your test route does not include a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show the correct steps at a practice location.

questions.question: Your horn should be used to:

options.text: Show other drivers you are angry.
Alert other drivers that you are nearby.
Scare other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alert other drivers that you are nearby.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn others of your presence. Only use it when necessary because it can startle other drivers and create danger.

questions.question: Driving at night is usually:

options.text: Harder than driving during the day.
Easier than driving during the day.
Not recommended.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than driving during the day.
questions.explanation: Night driving is harder because you cannot see hazards as well, headlight glare affects your vision, and tired drivers are more common on the road at night.

questions.question: Engine belts should:

options.text: Be frayed.
Not be worn too much.
Be greasy.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not be worn too much.
questions.explanation: Check engine belts for tightness and excessive wear. The right amount of give varies by vehicle, so learn what is safe for your vehicle.

questions.question: When parking parallel, you should:

options.text: Back up past the space, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
Pull forward directly into the space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space first, then back into it. Get your vehicle's rear as close to the rear of the space as possible. Your vehicle must fit completely within the space.

questions.question: When should you sign a vehicle inspection report?

options.text: After every trip
When problems have been fixed
After each fueling

questions.correctAnswerText: When problems have been fixed
questions.explanation: Sign a vehicle inspection report only if problems were found and either fixed or confirmed as not needing repair.

questions.question: When checking windshield wipers, the blades should be:

options.text: Soft.
Tight and in place.
Hard and brittle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tight and in place.
questions.explanation: Check wiper blades for damage, stiff rubber, and that they are secure. Clean the blades if they are dirty.

questions.question: Which is an example of required emergency equipment?

options.text: A spare electrical fuse
A loud horn
A battery-powered flashlight

questions.correctAnswerText: A spare electrical fuse
questions.explanation: All commercial vehicles must have proper emergency equipment. This includes spare electrical fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one working fire extinguisher.
